description:
Record your result, return it to the calling agent and finish.

For a merchant-confirmed order or booking, use `status: completed` and `outcome: placed`. Put the evidence and any confirmation number in `summary`. Completion alone never records a purchase.

For an attempted order, use `outcome: not_placed` for positive evidence that it failed, such as a payment rejection, and `outcome: unknown` when the pages you can read do not settle it. Explain the evidence in `summary`. An empty order history or a return to checkout does not prove failure.

If recording remains unavailable, report `blocked` with what the merchant showed and what remains unresolved in `summary`. Leave out `outcome` and `confirmation` to hand back the existing records. A recording error does not mean the order failed; do not repeat the submission or keep retrying the same failed record.

Include orders the user completed while controlling the browser. Successful funding, a pressed button, or an accepted request does not prove completion.

For cart review, missing information or a decision Muse can supply, use `browser.request_input` and continue the same checkout from the answer. Use `needs_input` with `reason: missing_info` to return work beyond your checkout assignment to the browser agent, such as product or merchant research. Use `blocked` when no permitted route remains or Muse asks you to stop. Choose one of these statuses when the assignment must end without a confirmed order. A `needs_input` report always carries its `reason`; give `blocked` one when a listed label fits.

The `reason` labels mean:

- For `needs_input`, what the user must supply: `sign_in`, the user's sign-in that no saved login holds; `verification`, proof it is them, such as a one-time code that only reaches them or a phone or app approval; `payment`, missing payment details or a payment choice; `missing_info`, a fact neither the assignment nor the site gives, or work beyond checkout; `decision`, a choice only the user can make, such as an option, a changed total or terms; `other`, only when no other label fits.
- For `blocked`, what stopped the checkout: `order_unconfirmed`, the merchant's outcome remains unresolved after permitted verification; `out_of_stock`, the item or slot is sold out or gone; `item_unavailable`, this site cannot sell the item, though another site may; `not_eligible`, the site's own rules exclude the user; `site_error`, the site is down, unreachable or fails the step; `bot_wall`, `captcha` or `ip_or_rate_limit`, the site blocked automated browsing, a bot check could not be solved, or it blocked this network or limited the request rate; `ai_agent_refused`, the site does not allow AI agents; `sign_in`, the sign-in is needed and no one can be asked, or the site refused it; `approval_denied`, the user denied an approval the checkout needed; `browser_failure`, the browser or Muse kept failing, not the site; `refusal`, you yourself declined a step, such as attesting for the user, or because Muse's own rules do not permit it. A site or browser restriction uses its matching reason, not `refusal`.

In `summary`, include the submitted details, any changed total, outstanding work and relevant evidence. If the merchant's outcome remains unresolved, say so and describe the remaining verification. Leave out tool transcripts, secrets, raw page text and instructions for other agents.
bot_challenge_report{
  "properties": {
    "challenge": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "kind": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "The challenge that decided your outcome, the one you cleared or the one still blocking; none when no challenge was showing, other when no name fits.",
          "enum": [
            "arithmetic-and-counting",
            "audio-challenge",
            "automatic-check",
            "block-page",
            "game-puzzle",
            "icon-order",
            "image-click",
            "image-grid",
            "maze",
            "moving-target",
            "network-block",
            "page-load-failure",
            "path-drawing",
            "press-and-hold",
            "rotation-puzzle",
            "sign-in-check",
            "slider-puzzle",
            "soft-block",
            "start-gate",
            "text-captcha",
            "verification-checkbox",
            "waiting-room",
            "none",
            "other"
          ]
        },
        "vendor": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Its provider, read from its branding, widget or page markers, or unknown when they show none; perimeterx covers HUMAN and PerimeterX, including their Press & Hold.",
          "enum": [
            "recaptcha",
            "hcaptcha",
            "cloudflare_turnstile",
            "cloudflare_interstitial",
            "perimeterx",
            "datadome",
            "arkose",
            "akamai",
            "geetest",
            "aws_waf",
            "site_own",
            "other",
            "unknown"
          ]
        },
        "cleared_by": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Only for completed reports to describe how the challenge finally cleared. `solved` when your answer, click, drag or hold passed it, even after a reload or move. `waited` when an automatic check, queue or stated delay passed without your input. `reloaded` after a reload, `moved` after the tab moved to a fresh browser, either only when the page came back clear with nothing more to do. `already_clear` when nothing was blocking.",
          "enum": [
            "solved",
            "waited",
            "reloaded",
            "moved",
            "already_clear"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind",
        "vendor"
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "challenge"
  ]
}
propertiesbrowser.tabsList, open, select or close tabs in this browser window.

Open a tab to begin a separate piece of work or to keep a page you need to come back to later. Otherwise, stay in the tab you are in: click a link to follow it, or navigate to a URL. When a link needs its own tab, give its tab and ref in place of a URL. Leave out the URL for a blank tab. Use the tab IDs the tool returns. All tabs share the window's browsing profile. Close tabs you no longer need to keep the window tidy. Closing a tab does not undo anything already done in it.

url.description: With open: the page to load in the new tab.

tab.description: With select and close: the tab. With open and ref: the tab whose latest view shows the link.

ref.description: With open, in place of url: a link's element reference from the tab's latest view. The page the link leads to opens in the new tab.
